key_insight: Existing general-purpose ML interatomic potentials do not reliably transfer to heterogeneous catalysis, so catalysis-specific benchmarking is needed to judge real predictive value.
engineering_relevance: For catalyst design and screening, these models can be useful for surface energetics and some barriers, but adsorption and site preferences still need careful validation against DFT.
method: Built HetCat26, a benchmark suite for heterogeneous catalysis covering surfaces, metal/oxide interactions, adsorption, and reaction networks.
Evaluated 15 pre-trained foundation MLIPs against catalysis-specific tests.
Compared performance on HetCat26 with broader materials benchmarks and training-data consistency effects.
evidence_signal: Across HetCat26, the study found good performance for surface energetics and some reaction barriers, but larger errors for adsorption and frequent failures to reproduce DFT site preferences; two models stood out as consistently accurate.
watch_item: Do not mix PBE and PBE+U data in the same training set, as inconsistent reference data can degrade transferability and benchmarking reliability.
paper_title: Assessing the Transferability of General-Purpose MachineLearning Interatomic Potentials for Heterogeneous Catalysis with HetCat26
